19 Pounds in Five Hours: Merab Dvalishvili Rehydrates and Promises to “Eat” Petr Yan
NewsOctober 23, 20262 min readRédaction Next Fight
- Merab Dvalishvili weighed 135 pounds at Friday’s UFC 333 weigh-ins, then 154 pounds five hours later.
- The Georgian, who said Wednesday he still had five kilos to lose, put 19 pounds back on by drinking water.
- He faces Petr Yan on Saturday in Abu Dhabi for the bantamweight title, with the trilogy tied at one win apiece.
Right on 135 at Friday morning’s UFC 333 weigh-ins, 154 five hours later: Merab Dvalishvili filmed his rehydration, and he has already let Petr Yan know he’s next on the menu.
On Friday morning in Abu Dhabi, Merab Dvalishvili hit the number exactly: 135 pounds, the bantamweight championship limit, same as Petr Yan. Five hours later he was back on a scale, phone camera rolling. The reading: 154 pounds. “It’s been only five hours since I made weight and I’m back already,” he said in a video posted to his X account. “I’ve been drinking water… In only five hours I gained back 19 pounds.” That’s 19 pounds before his first real meal.
“Tomorrow you guys already know who I’m gonna eat”
The rest of the plan fits in one line: “Now I’m gonna start eating. Let’s go, it’s food fest, and tomorrow you guys already know who I’m gonna eat.” The main course is Petr Yan, whom he meets Saturday in the co-main event of UFC 333 with the bantamweight title on the line.
Five kilos in two days, 19 pounds back in a morning
The rest of the weigh-ins went off without drama, with one exception: Nicolle Caliari came in at 120.5 pounds for a 116-pound strawweight limit and forfeits 30 percent of her purse. In the main event, Alexander Volkanovski (144.5) and Movsar Evloev (145) both made weight.
Yan (20-5) and Dvalishvili (21-5) are one win apiece. The Georgian smothered the Russian in March 2023, 50-45 on all three cards. Yan took the belt back at UFC 323 in December 2025 (49-46, 49-46, 48-47), snapping a 14-fight winning streak along the way. Dvalishvili believes he fought his opponent’s fight that night and vows to go back to his own: here’s what he plans to change for the trilogy.
UFC 333 takes place Saturday, October 24 at Etihad Arena. The main card starts at 2 p.m. ET (11 a.m. PT) on Paramount+ in the U.S., with Yan vs. Dvalishvili right before Volkanovski vs. Evloev. Every start time is in our viewing guide.

Dvalishvili made his UFC debut on December 9, 2017, against Frankie Saenz at UFC Fight Night: Swanson vs. Ortega.[19] He lost the fight via split decision.[20] 10 out of 13 media outlets scored the bout for Dvalishvili.[21]
Dvalishvili faced former UFC Bantamweight champion Petr Yan on March 11, 2023, at UFC Fight Night: Yan vs. Dvalishvili.[51] He won the fight via unanimous decision. Dvalishvili broke the UFC record for most takedowns attempted in a single bout with 49 attempts.[52][53]
Dvalishvili made his first title defense against undefeated contender Umar Nurmagomedov on January 18, 2025, at UFC 311.[58] He won the fight by unanimous decision.[59] This fight earned him another Fight of the Night award.[60] Dvalishvili broke the record for most takedowns landed in UFC history with 92.[61]
For his fourth title defense, Dvalishvili rematched former champion Petr Yan at UFC 323 on December 6, 2025.[67] With a win, Dvalishvili would become the first UFC champion in history to defend a title four times in the same calendar year.[67] He lost the championship by unanimous decision.[68] This fight earned him another Fight of the Night award.[69]
Dvalishvili is scheduled to face Yan in a trilogy bout for the championship on October 24, 2026 at UFC 333.[70]

What is Merab Dvalishvili’s professional record?
The last loss for Dvalishvili was a split decision to Ricky Simon at UFC Fight Night 151 in April 2019 (UFC Stats). Many fans and analysts disputed the scoring, arguing Dvalishvili did enough to win, which fueled his later motivation.
What happened in Merab Dvalishvili’s last loss?
The fight went the distance with Simon getting the nod from two judges. Dvalishvili outlanded Simon in total strikes 80–65 (UFC Stats).
What is Merab Dvalishvili’s fighting style and statistics?
Merab Dvalishvili fights out of the orthodox stance and relies on relentless pace, takedowns, and superior cardio (UFC Stats). He averages 4.42 significant strikes per minute and has a takedown defense rate that keeps opponents guessing.
What is Merab Dvalishvili’s height and reach?
His style is built on pressure. In the rematch with Petr Yan at UFC 323, Dvalishvili attempted 29 takedowns, landed 2, and controlled the fight for 5 minutes 12 seconds (UFC Stats). He also attempted 2 submissions. His cardio allows him to maintain that pace through five rounds.
What is Merab Dvalishvili’s next fight and career timeline?
As of 2025, Merab Dvalishvili is the reigning bantamweight champion. His next fight is expected to be a title defense (opponent TBD) (ESPN). He won the title at UFC 306 in September 2024 by submission over Sean O’Malley.

sources.excerpt:
The scorecards from UFC 323 told the real story: Petr Yan stopped 27 of Merab Dvalishvili’s 29 takedown attempts. Not 10. Not 15. Twenty-seven. That one number captures both the genius of Merab’s system and the only fighter who ever truly solved it. For 14 straight UFC fights across six years, nobody even came close. Understanding why Dvalishvili dominated — and why Yan was the exception — tells you more about modern MMA than most fighters communicate in an entire career.
The Foundation: Merab Dvalishvili’s Takedown Volume Has No Peer in UFC History
Merab Dvalishvili attempts more takedowns per minute than any fighter in any weight class in UFC history. Not a bantamweight record. A universal record across the entire promotion. He grew up in Georgia competing in folk wrestling, freestyle wrestling, and combat sambo — disciplines that reward relentless offensive pressure over technical perfection. By the time he entered the UFC in 2017, he had spent over a decade building a grappling engine designed to run at 100 percent and never shut off.
How Petr Yan Cracked the System at UFC 323
Three things dismantled Merab on December 6, 2025 at T-Mobile Arena. First, Yan’s footwork was exceptional — he maintained the range where Merab’s entries required longer, slower shots that were easier to read and time. Second, Yan’s sprawl defense was punishing. He wasn’t simply stuffing takedowns; he was landing hard shots from every scramble, accumulating damage on every failed attempt from Merab. Third — and nobody predicted this — Yan won the takedown battle 5-2.
Is Merab Dvalishvili the best wrestler in UFC bantamweight history?
Who beat Merab Dvalishvili for the UFC Bantamweight title?
Petr Yan recaptured the belt at UFC 323 in December 2025, winning by decision with scores of 49-46, 49-46, and 48-47. Yan stopped 27 of Merab’s 29 takedown attempts and also won the takedown battle 5-2, ending Dvalishvili’s 14-fight UFC win streak.
What is Merab Dvalishvili’s career record?
As of 2026, Merab Dvalishvili’s professional record stands at 21-5. His UFC tenure included a 14-fight winning streak from 2019 to 2025, with victories over José Aldo, Henry Cejudo, Petr Yan, Sean O’Malley (twice), and Umar Nurmagomedov along the way.

- The Georgian, who said Wednesday he still had five kilos to lose, put 19 pounds back on by drinking water.
- He faces Petr Yan on Saturday in Abu Dhabi for the bantamweight title, with the trilogy tied at one win apiece.
Right on 135 at Friday morning’s UFC 333 weigh-ins, 154 five hours later: Merab Dvalishvili filmed his rehydration, and he has already let Petr Yan know he’s next on the menu.
On Friday morning in Abu Dhabi, Merab Dvalishvili hit the number exactly: 135 pounds, the bantamweight championship limit, same as Petr Yan. Five hours later he was back on a scale, phone camera rolling. The reading: 154 pounds. “It’s been only five hours since I made weight and I’m back already,” he said in a video posted to his X account. “I’ve been drinking water… In only five hours I gained back 19 pounds.” That’s 19 pounds before his first real meal.
“Tomorrow you guys already know who I’m gonna eat”
The rest of the plan fits in one line: “Now I’m gonna start eating. Let’s go, it’s food fest, and tomorrow you guys already know who I’m gonna eat.” The main course is Petr Yan, whom he meets Saturday in the co-main event of UFC 333 with the bantamweight title on the line.
Five kilos in two days, 19 pounds back in a morning
The rest of the weigh-ins went off without drama, with one exception: Nicolle Caliari came in at 120.5 pounds for a 116-pound strawweight limit and forfeits 30 percent of her purse. In the main event, Alexander Volkanovski (144.5) and Movsar Evloev (145) both made weight.
Yan (20-5) and Dvalishvili (21-5) are one win apiece. The Georgian smothered the Russian in March 2023, 50-45 on all three cards. Yan took the belt back at UFC 323 in December 2025 (49-46, 49-46, 48-47), snapping a 14-fight winning streak along the way. Dvalishvili believes he fought his opponent’s fight that night and vows to go back to his own: here’s what he plans to change for the trilogy.
UFC 333 takes place Saturday, October 24 at Etihad Arena. The main card starts at 2 p.m. ET (11 a.m. PT) on Paramount+ in the U.S., with Yan vs. Dvalishvili right before Volkanovski vs. Evloev. Every start time is in our viewing guide.

Dvalishvili made his UFC debut on December 9, 2017, against Frankie Saenz at UFC Fight Night: Swanson vs. Ortega.[19] He lost the fight via split decision.[20] 10 out of 13 media outlets scored the bout for Dvalishvili.[21]

Dvalishvili made his first title defense against undefeated contender Umar Nurmagomedov on January 18, 2025, at UFC 311.[58] He won the fight by unanimous decision.[59] This fight earned him another Fight of the Night award.[60] Dvalishvili broke the record for most takedowns landed in UFC history with 92.[61]
For his fourth title defense, Dvalishvili rematched former champion Petr Yan at UFC 323 on December 6, 2025.[67] With a win, Dvalishvili would become the first UFC champion in history to defend a title four times in the same calendar year.[67] He lost the championship by unanimous decision.[68] This fight earned him another Fight of the Night award.[69]

The scorecards from UFC 323 told the real story: Petr Yan stopped 27 of Merab Dvalishvili’s 29 takedown attempts. Not 10. Not 15. Twenty-seven. That one number captures both the genius of Merab’s system and the only fighter who ever truly solved it. For 14 straight UFC fights across six years, nobody even came close. Understanding why Dvalishvili dominated — and why Yan was the exception — tells you more about modern MMA than most fighters communicate in an entire career.
The Foundation: Merab Dvalishvili’s Takedown Volume Has No Peer in UFC History
Merab Dvalishvili attempts more takedowns per minute than any fighter in any weight class in UFC history. Not a bantamweight record. A universal record across the entire promotion. He grew up in Georgia competing in folk wrestling, freestyle wrestling, and combat sambo — disciplines that reward relentless offensive pressure over technical perfection. By the time he entered the UFC in 2017, he had spent over a decade building a grappling engine designed to run at 100 percent and never shut off.
How Petr Yan Cracked the System at UFC 323
Three things dismantled Merab on December 6, 2025 at T-Mobile Arena. First, Yan’s footwork was exceptional — he maintained the range where Merab’s entries required longer, slower shots that were easier to read and time. Second, Yan’s sprawl defense was punishing. He wasn’t simply stuffing takedowns; he was landing hard shots from every scramble, accumulating damage on every failed attempt from Merab. Third — and nobody predicted this — Yan won the takedown battle 5-2.

Who beat Merab Dvalishvili for the UFC Bantamweight title?
Petr Yan recaptured the belt at UFC 323 in December 2025, winning by decision with scores of 49-46, 49-46, and 48-47. Yan stopped 27 of Merab’s 29 takedown attempts and also won the takedown battle 5-2, ending Dvalishvili’s 14-fight UFC win streak.
What is Merab Dvalishvili’s career record?
As of 2026, Merab Dvalishvili’s professional record stands at 21-5. His UFC tenure included a 14-fight winning streak from 2019 to 2025, with victories over José Aldo, Henry Cejudo, Petr Yan, Sean O’Malley (twice), and Umar Nurmagomedov along the way.
